title: The Lifecycle of a Click: From Buy to Optimistic UI
summary: This lesson breaks down the six-step process of a network request, from frontend validation to database atomicity. It also introduces Optimistic UI, explaining when to provide instant feedback and when to make the user wait for server confirmation.

transcript.text: You click Buy. Six things happen before the spinner stops.
One, your browser validates the form. No network yet. Instant feedback is a frontend job.
Two, the request leaves. One JSON payload, headers, and a token that proves who you are.
Three, the backend validates everything again. Client input is never trusted. Anyone can forge a request.
Four, business logic runs. Stock check, price check, payment charge.
Five, the database writes your order. One transaction wraps every row. All of them commit, or none of them do. That's atomicity.
Six, the response rides back. Status 200 and the order ID the server created. The spinner stops. Your UI repaints with server truth, not a guess.
The twist - Optimistic UI. Fast apps cheat. A like, a favorite, a rename. Repaint instantly, reconcile later.
But money is not optimistic. Your payment earns the spinner. That's the full round trip.
Follow for more under-the-UI breakdowns, save this for your next feature.
